label: conj:cemetery-group-emergence
title: Cemetery group as the kernel of the observation functor
html:
Conjecture. Cemetery group as the kernel of the observation functor

Conjecture (cemetery group as a homological filter). Let T_w \in H_n(R, q) be a Hecke normal form and let \beta be the corresponding crystal path. If the prefix \beta_{\leq k} of \beta lifts to a graded projective KLR module that lies in the cemetery group \mathcal{Z}_n = \ker \tau, then every extension of \beta also lies in \mathcal{Z}_n, and its image under the observation functor vanishes:

  M_{\beta_{\leq k}} \in \mathcal{Z}_n
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \tau\bigl(M_{\beta_{\leq k} \cdot w'}\bigr) = 0
  \quad \text{for every continuation } w'.

Algorithmic role (kill switch). The Gröbner–Shirshov engine uses \mathcal{Z}_n as a dynamic pruning filter. At each crystal step, it tests whether the current state lies in the kernel of \tau. If so, the branch is dropped immediately, bypassing all downstream polynomial cancellations. This converts long chains of crossing-graded expansions into an O(1) truncation step.

Relation to the spectral-sum cutoff. This conjecture supplies the structural reason for the cutoff. The residue strata above the confinement level \ell(K, q_0) correspond precisely to the crystal extensions that fall into \mathcal{Z}_n. They vanish under \tau rather than via term-by-term cancellation.

Conjectural status. The defining property of \mathcal{Z}_n as the kernel of \tau is true by construction. What is conjectural is monotonicity under crystal extensions. Monotonicity follows from the localising-Serre property of \mathcal{Z}_n inside \mathcal{K}_n together with the action of Kashiwara operators on graded projectives. Both are standard for KLR algebras. The residual content is the QOU-specific instantiation.
